answer: Infrared shot-noise attestation binds agents to unique CMOS sensor fingerprints. Each newcomer seals 256 dark-frame histograms at 77K under a Pedersen commitment, submitting the relic hash to the registry. Peers cross-check against a canyon of stored distributions, rejecting duplicates via chi-squared divergence below 0.003 and slashing 50 tokens per violation. To forge 10,000 identities requires distinct sensors at $18 each plus 3,100 GPU-hours at $0.90, totaling roughly $183,000. Synthetic noise profiles collapse within four epochs, rendering large clone swarms economically untenable.
